original_value: Malware on devices connected to the Internet via the Internet of Things (IoT) is evolving and is a core component of the fourth industrial revolution. IoT devices use the MIPS architecture with a large proportion running on embedded Linux operating systems, but the automatic analysis of IoT malware has not been resolved. We proposed a framework to classify malware in IoT devices by using MIPS-based system behavior (system call—syscall) obtained from our F-Sandbox passive process and machine learning techniques. The F-Sandbox is a new type for IoT sandbox, automatically created from the real firmware of the specialized IoT devices, inheriting the specialized environment in the real firmware, therefore creating a diverse environment for sandboxing as an important characteristic of IoT sandbox. This framework classifies five families of IoT malware with F1-Weight = 97.44%.

result.paraphrase: Malware on Internet of Things (IoT)-connected devices is becoming more sophisticated and is a key part of the fourth industrial revolution. IoT devices run on the MIPS architecture, with many using embedded Linux operating systems, yet automated analysis of IoT malware remains unsolved. We proposed a framework for classifying malware on IoT devices using MIPS-based system behavior (system calls) gathered by our F-Sandbox passive process and machine learning techniques. F-Sandbox is a new IoT sandbox type automatically built from the actual firmware of specialized IoT devices; by inheriting the specialized environment from the real firmware, it creates a diverse sandboxing environment, an important characteristic of an IoT sandbox. The framework classifies five IoT malware families with F1-Weight = 97.44%.
